Subaru China Recalls Nearly 200,000 Older Models Over Wiring Issue
13 photos
Photo: Subaru
As you're well aware, the steering wheel of a modern automobile does a lot more than simply turn the front wheels. It carries a surprisingly large collection of electrical functions, and 'electrical' is the key word here. Per the Subaru brand's latest recall, a guide inside the steering wheel's spiral cable may damage internal wiring.
This failure concerns up to 196,494 imported vehicles in the Chinese market, and such a failure leaves the horn inoperable. According to the recall documentation filed with the State Administration for Market Regulation, the folks at Subaru Automobile expect the campaign to start on December 21, 2026.
S2026M0135I is what Subaru Automobile calls the campaign, which covers BRZ , XV, Outback, Legacy, and Forester models produced from August 23, 2011, through August 25, 2016. Better known as a clock spring or steering roll connector, the subject component is referred to as a spiral cable in the Chinese-market notice.
Its job is pretty straightforward. When the steering wheel rotates, the electrical connections need to link it to the stationary wiring in the steering column. A flexible coiled conductor allows steering wheel movement without forcing regular wires to twist around the column every time someone negotiates a roundabout.
Subaru Automobile highlights that internal guides may lead to an internal failure, which means that said guides cause premature wear of the internal wiring. Most surprisingly, the filing published by the SAMR does not mention associated failures of the steering wheel airbag, power steering, or any other systems.
Photo: Subaru The Japanese automaker has dealt with similar problems before, albeit the older campaigns involved different production dates and componentry. Back in 2010, for example, both the Legacy and Outback were recalled in the US with the blessing of the NHTSA due to steering column roll connectors that could break.
Said condition disables the horn, steering wheel airbag, cruise control switches, radio controls, and the paddle shifters, if equipped. Subaru of America instructed US-market dealers at the time to inspect the connector's production lot number. Suspect connectors were replaced at no charge to affected owners and lessees.
A corresponding recall was published by the Japanese regulator, and its filing identified variations in the grease applied to the roll connector's flat cable. In other words, those connectors were susceptible to breaking due to chemical stress cracks.
Australia has relevant context as well, with Subaru Australia recalling the Impreza, XV, and Forester as part of campaign SRT-215 for wiring that could wear prematurely due to contact with a metal plate inside the steering column surround. The affected circuits included the horn and steering wheel controls. In extreme circumstances, a short could interrupt power to the engine control unit.
Turning our attention back to the Chinese recall, the company will contact affected customers by telephone, SMS, and via WeChat. Those who prefer taking matters into their own hands may contact Subaru Automobile directly or their preferred retailers for more information.
Via // SAMR
